record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: In the multiserver job model, where jobs may request different numbers of servers and may have different service-time distributions, what is the exact stability region beyond the currently understood special cases such as identical exponential durations or the two-class exponential case?

evidence.quote: Very recently, Grosof et al. [82] derived a simple closed-form expression for the stability region of the multiserver job model where jobs have different exponential service time durations. Unfortunately, the work in [82] is limited to the case of only two classes. Characterizing the stability region in a more general setting is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous-time multiserver-job queueing model defined as follows. There are k servers and J classes of jobs. Class-j jobs arrive according to independent Poisson processes with rates λ_j (j = 1, ..., J), each class-j job requires simultaneous use of exactly s_j ∈ {1, ..., k} servers for the entire duration of its service, and class-j service times are i.i.d. samples from a distribution F_j with mean 1/μ_j. Jobs are served in first-come-first-served (FCFS) order: the head-of-line job waits until s_j servers become simultaneously available, and jobs may pass one another only when blocked by capacity. A job in service cannot be preempted, and idle servers cannot work on waiting jobs that need more servers than currently available.

Define the system to be stable if the number-in-system process is positive recurrent. Determine, in closed form, the exact stability region — that is, the set of arrival-rate vectors (λ_1, ..., λ_J) for which the system is stable — as a function of (k, {s_j}, {F_j}, {μ_j}), in the general setting of arbitrarily many classes J ≥ 2 with possibly distinct server requirements s_j and possibly non-exponential service-time distributions F_j.

(Known special cases include: (i) all classes share a common exponential service-time distribution but may have different server requirements; (ii) J = 2 classes with class-dependent exponential service-time distributions. The problem asks for the characterization in the remaining general cases.)
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Grosof, Harchol-Balter, and Scheller-Wolf ("New Stability Results for Multiserver-Job Models via Product-form Saturated Systems", MAMA/SIGMETRICS PER, 2023) extends stability characterizations beyond the two-class exponential case using product-form saturated systems, but a fully general closed-form characterization for arbitrary numbers of classes with distinct (and possibly non-exponential) service distributions is not yet available. The problem remains open in full generality, with active partial progress.

status_evidence.title: New Stability Results for Multiserver-job Models via Product-form Saturated Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Product-form saturated systems used to derive new stability results for multiserver-job models beyond previously known cases.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extensions beyond the two-class exponential setting exist but do not give a fully general closed-form stability region.

status_evidence.title: Stability for Two-class Multiserver-job Systems (arXiv:2010.00631)
status_evidence.snippet: Closed-form stability region for the two-class multiserver-job system with class-dependent exponential service times.
status_evidence.claim: The two-class exponential case is solved; general multi-class/non-exponential case is not.

status_evidence.title: The Multiserver-Job Stochastic Recurrence Equation for Cloud Computing Performance Evaluation
status_evidence.snippet: No general results for FCFS MJQM with arbitrary class counts and non-exponential service distributions; alternative tools (stochastic recurrence) are introduced.
status_evidence.claim: The general-case stability region remains an open problem.
